source_text:
Οὗτος γὰρ ἐκρύβη πρῶτον

μὲν ἐν κοιλίᾳ σαρκός, ἔπειτα δὲ ἐν κοιλίᾳ τῆς γῆς, ὅπου μὲν ἁγιάζων τοὺς
γεννωμένους διὰ τῆς κυήσεως, ὅπου δὲ ζωογονῶν τοὺς τεθανατωμένους διὰ τῆς
ἀναστάσεως· «Ἀπέδρα γὰρ ὀδύνη καὶ λύπη καὶ στεναγμός.» «Τίς γὰρ ἔγνω νοῦν
θεοῦ, ἢ τίς σύμβουλος αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο», ἀλλ' ἢ ὁ Λόγος ὁ σαρκωθεὶς καὶ ξύλῳ
προσηλωθεὶς καὶ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστὰς καὶ εἰς οὐρανοὺς ὑψωθείς;
6 Αὕτη ἡ ἡμέρα χαρᾶς εὐαγγελισμός· ἐν τῇ γὰρ ἡμέρᾳ ταύτῃ ἀνέστη ὁ κύριος
συνεγείρας τὴν τοῦ Ἀδὰμ ἀγέλην· ἐγεννήθη γὰρ διὰ τὸν ἄνθρωπον καὶ ἀνέστη ἐν τῷ
ἀνθρώπῳ. Σήμερον διὰ τὸν ἀναστάντα παράδεισος ἀνέῳκται καὶ Ἀδὰμ ζωογονεῖται
καὶ Εὔα παρηγορεῖται καὶ κλῆσις πληθύνεται καὶ βασιλεία ἑτοιμάζεται καὶ ἄνθρωπος
σῴζεται καὶ Χριστὸς προσκυνεῖται· καταπατήσας γὰρ τὸν θάνατον καὶ αἰχμαλωτίσας
τὸν τύραννον καὶ σκυλεύσας τὸν ᾅδην, ἀνέβη εἰς οὐρανούς, ὡς βα σιλεὺς
νενικηκώς, ὡς ἡγεμὼν ἔνδοξος, ὡς ἡνίοχος ἄλειπτος, λέ-γων τῷ Πατρί· «Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ
καὶ τὰ παιδία ἅ μοι δέδωκας, ὦ θεός», καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. Καὶ ἤκουσεν παρὰ τοῦ Πατρός·
«Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου.»
Αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα, νῦν καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.

2
thought_title: Hidden in flesh and earth, then raised and enthroned
orientation: Hesychius the preacher closes the homily by telling how Christ was hidden in flesh and in the earth and then rose and ascended to present the redeemed to the Father.
pass_a_gloss: For this one was hidden first in a belly of flesh, then in a belly of the earth, in the one place making holy the ones being born through the pregnancy, and in the other place giving life to the ones having been put to death through the resurrection; 'For pain and grief and groaning fled away.' 'For who knew mind of God, or who became counselor of him,' except the Word the one having been made flesh and having been nailed to wood and having risen from dead ones and having been lifted up into heavens? This day is good news of joy; for in this day the lord rose having raised together with himself the flock of Adam; for he was born on account of the human being and he rose in the human being. Today on account of the one having risen paradise has been opened and Adam is given life and Eve is comforted and calling is multiplied and kingdom is prepared and human being is saved and Christ is worshiped; for having trampled down death and having taken captive the tyrant and having plundered Hades, he went up into heavens, as king having won, as glorious commander, as unbeaten charioteer, saying to the Father: 'Behold I and the children which to me you have given, O God,' and the things following. And he heard from the Father: 'Sit at right hands of me until I place the enemies of you as footstool of the feet of you.' To him be the glory, now and into the ages of the ages. Amen.

choices.english: belly of flesh ... belly of the earth
choices.why: keeps the same literal noun in both halves to preserve the parallel womb-flesh / womb-earth

choices.english: in the one place ... in the other place
choices.why: renders the correlative contrast of the two hidings, not two different places named in the text
source has ξύλον, not σταυρός, so literal wood keeps the distinction
keeps perfect participle force and brief glossary sense victory rather than generic triumph
literal passive of πληθύνω with abstract subject κλῆσις, without adding church or elect

pass_b_english: For he was hidden first in the belly of flesh, and then in the belly of the earth. In the one place he made holy those who are born, through his conception; in the other place he gave life to those who had died, through the resurrection. For, as Scripture says, “Pain and grief and sighing have fled away” (Isaiah 35:10). For “who has known the mind of God, or who has become his counselor” (Romans 11:34), if not the Word who became flesh and was nailed to wood and rose from the dead and was lifted into the heavens?

This day is the good news of joy. For on this day the Lord rose, raising Adam’s flock with himself. For he was born for man, and he rose in man. Today, through the one who rose, paradise has been opened, and Adam is given life, and Eve is comforted, and calling is multiplied, and the kingdom is prepared, and man is saved, and Christ is worshiped. For after trampling down death and taking the tyrant captive and plundering Hades, he went up into the heavens as king who has won the victory, as glorious commander, as unbeaten charioteer. He says to the Father, “Here I am and the children you have given me, O God” (Hebrews 2:13), and the rest. And he heard from the Father in answer, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet” (Psalm 110:1). To him be glory, now and to the ages of ages, Amen.
notes: source line-breaks split βα σιλεὺς and λέ-γων; read as βασιλεὺς and λέγων; trailing 2 is a page or section number, not text
